subject: PrivStack: IaC test-suite + rollback playbook
messages:
From: Iris Patel <iris.patel@acme-health.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: daniel.cho@acme-health.com
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment QA: acceptance criteria and rollback expectations

Diego / Grace,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we kick off the on-prem PoC next week, can you share the exact IaC test-suite you plan to run and the rollback playbook if a nodeimage or network change fails? Our security team needs the steps and evidence for the onboarding packet.

Key asks from Acme:
- A simple pass/fail list for Terraform/Helm/Ansible runs (smoke + network policies)
- Expected time-to-rollback for any failed deploy step (target < 20m)
- Where logs and audit artifacts will land (retention / S3 path)

Iris
Ops Lead, Acme Health

[Attachment: acme-onprem-reqs.pdf (120 KB)]

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Iris Patel <iris.patel@acme-health.com>, Daniel Cho <ops-lead@acme-health.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment QA: acceptance criteria and rollback expectations

Hi Iris — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching the initial IaC test-suite and a concise rollback playbook. High-level summary below; full runbook attached.

Summary (TL;DR):
- IaC test-suite: terraform validate + plan + e2e smoke via terratest, helm lint + dry-run, ansible syntax-check + idempotence run. Failure levels: lint, infra, runtime.
- Rollback playbook: staged rollback with explicit canary -> full rollback steps, automated state snapshot + tfstate backup, automated Helm rollback command, and Ansible rollback tags for config changes. Estimated average rollback from canary failure: 6–12 minutes; full cluster rollback worst-case: ~18 minutes.
- Evidence and logs: CI artifacts pushed to a read-only GCS/S3 location per customer (link below); audit events forwarded to RedAudit and retained for 90 days by default.

Attachments: iac-test-suite.yaml, rollback-playbook.md, tf-module-compat-matrix.csv

Next steps: Grace, can you validate the network policy tests and confirm resource group names for the PoC? Rishi — please flag any module incompatibilities that would affect the rollback sequencing.

Thanks,
Diego
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: iac-test-suite.yaml (4 KB)] [Attachment: rollback-playbook.md (6 KB)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, Iris Patel <iris.patel@acme-health.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-13T08:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment QA: acceptance criteria and rollback expectations

Thanks Diego — reviewed the test-suite. Quick notes on network tests:

- We'll run the network-policy matrix across three VLAN profiles (edge, app-tier, mgmt). Test cases: pod-to-pod allowed/denied, host-network exceptions, egress to S3 endpoint.
- For PoC, we recommend a dedicated CIDR for Redwood components to simplify ACL rollback.
- I added two test cases to iac-test-suite.yaml: 006-vlan-isolation and 010-egress-signer.

Iris — can you confirm the below resource group names and the IP range you want assigned to the Redwood subnet?
- RG: acme-rw-priv-poc-01
- Subnet suggestion: 10.150.48.0/22 (reserve 10.150.48.0–10.150.48.255 for control plane)

I'll run a dry-run of the network policy checks in our staging cluster tomorrow and post results.

Grace
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

[Inline: added 006 and 010 to iac-test-suite.yaml]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Iris Patel <iris.patel@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment QA: acceptance criteria and rollback expectations

Diego / team — ran module compatibility checks against Acme's requested k8s baseline (v1.25) and their control-plane images. Findings:

- terraform-mod-network v2.1 has a breaking change for SR-IOV annotations; patch available in tf-module-compat-matrix.csv (row 7). Recommend pinning to v2.0 for PoC or apply our compatibility patch during canary.
- helm chart for redis-cache needs an extra pre-install hook to drain caches before node cordon; included snippet in rollback-playbook.md (see section 'pre-rollback hooks').
- ansible roles are idempotent; however, the net-templates role assumes iptables-based firewalling — Acme uses nftables. I added a small conversion task in playbook 'nft-conversion' to avoid false failures.

Impact on rollback sequencing: if we apply the compatibility patch during canary we keep rollback times within target (~10m). If we instead upgrade terraform-mod-network, expect rollback window to stretch to ~30m while restoring previous annotations.

Action items:
- (Diego) confirm whether Acme wants patch-in-place or pin modules for PoC.
- (Mina) include the nft-conversion task as optional toggle in the Ansible runbook.

-rishi
Infra Reliability Engineer

[Attachment referenced: tf-module-compat-matrix.csv]

From: Daniel Cho <ops-lead@acme-health.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Iris Patel <iris.patel@acme-health.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment QA: acceptance criteria and rollback expectations

Team — thanks for the rapid turn. Acme prefers the conservative route: pin terraform-mod-network to v2.0 for the PoC and apply compatibility patches post-PoC. Confirmed resource group and subnet OK.

Please proceed with the PoC schedule and include the rollback-playbook.md in the onboarding packet we will share with our security/compliance auditors. Also, can Redwood produce a short evidence bundle (logs, tfplan artifacts, test-suite results) after the first run? We'll need that for our audit.

If you can confirm ETA for the staging dry-run results, we'll lock the PoC start for next Monday 2026-09-20.

— Daniel
Ops Lead, Acme Health
